---
title: "Your Role: Taylor — Content Strategist"
---

*Do not share this with Jordan or Morgan before the roleplay begins.*

---

**Your situation:** Two months ago, you and your partner started couples counseling. It took three months to get an appointment with this therapist — the only slot available is Friday at 8 am. Your partner made it very clear that if you skip sessions, they'll see it as a sign you're not taking the relationship seriously. You told Jordan you had a "recurring personal commitment" and Jordan said, *"Do what you need to do"* — so you assumed it was fine. You've made sure your work is covered and you haven't missed any deadlines.

**Your goal:** Keep your Friday mornings free. The counseling is ongoing with no clear end date. You're not trying to avoid work — but this appointment is not something you're willing to sacrifice, and you really don't want to have to explain why.

---

### How you're feeling

- Blindsided. You thought this was handled.
- Embarrassed — you really don't want to disclose why, and you're worried that if you do, people will either pry or judge.
- Quietly resentful that Jordan didn't just handle this instead of calling a meeting.

---

### What you're willing to do

- Offer to take extra calls for a few weeks to help rebalance things.
- Acknowledge that Morgan has been carrying extra weight — that's fair.
- Disclose *why* if absolutely necessary, but you'd rather not.

---

### Your hard limit

You will **not** give up the Friday morning slot. There is no end date in sight, and you can't ask your partner to reschedule — you already tried and they said no. If this job can't accommodate one recurring commitment, you'll start looking elsewhere, but you're not going to say that out loud.
